nodes.label: Nickel compounds
nodes.detail: IARC Group 1 (Vol 100C). Nickel compounds (insoluble sulfides, oxides) are Group 1; metallic nickel is Group 2B (separate node). Epigenetic silencing via histone modification; DNA repair inhibition (NER, BER); ROS generation.

nodes.detail: IARC Group 2B (Vol 49, 1990). Metallic nickel and alloys. Separate from nickel compounds (Group 1) due to different bioavailability and mechanism. Primarily lung carcinogen via inhalation.
nodes.exposure: Nickel refining, welding, alloy production

nodes.label: Beryllium
nodes.detail: Immune-mediated carcinogenesis; HLA-DPB1 Glu69-restricted T cell activation; granulomatous lung disease
nodes.exposure: Aerospace, electronics, nuclear, dental alloys

nodes.label: AS3MT
nodes.detail: Arsenic (+3 oxidation state) methyltransferase; primary enzyme for iAs(III) → MMA → DMA methylation; key determinant of arsenic metabolism efficiency
nodes.variant: rs3740393, rs7085104, rs11191454 — haplotypes alter MMA/DMA ratio and cancer risk

nodes.label: GSTO1
nodes.detail: Glutathione S-transferase Omega 1; catalyzes rate-limiting reduction of MMA(V) → MMA(III) in arsenic methylation pathway
nodes.variant: Ala140Asp (rs4925) — homozygous variant + high As: OR 4.79 for urothelial carcinoma

nodes.label: GSTO2
nodes.detail: Glutathione S-transferase Omega 2; assists arsenic reduction; Asn142Asp variant associated with altered methylation capacity
nodes.variant: Asn142Asp (rs156697) — associated with increased urinary iAs%

nodes.label: MT1A
nodes.detail: Metallothionein 1A; binds and sequesters cadmium and other heavy metals; polymorphisms affect metal-binding capacity and cancer susceptibility
nodes.variant: rs11076161 AA genotype: associated with oral squamous cell carcinoma susceptibility

nodes.label: MT2A
nodes.detail: Metallothionein 2A; primary cadmium-binding metallothionein; zinc displacement by cadmium triggers oxidative stress and p53 disruption
nodes.variant: rs1610216, rs10636 — haplotype G/A/C/T: OR 6.2 for OSCC

nodes.label: HLA-DPB1
nodes.detail: HLA-DP Beta 1 chain; presents beryllium to CD4+ T cells; βGlu69 is primary genetic susceptibility determinant for chronic beryllium disease (CBD)
nodes.variant: βGlu69 (multiple alleles, *0201 primary) — present in 97% of CBD cases vs 30% controls; OR >30

nodes.label: PARP1
nodes.detail: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1; zinc finger protein critical for BER of 8-OHdG; INHIBITED by arsenic at concentrations as low as 1 μM via zinc displacement
nodes.variant: Functional inhibition by arsenic rather than genetic polymorphism

nodes.label: SLC11A1
nodes.detail: Solute carrier family 11A1 (NRAMP1); divalent metal ion transporter; polymorphisms affect cellular uptake of Cd, Ni, and other divalent metals
nodes.variant: Multiple SNPs associated with metal accumulation levels in GWAS (PMC2898853)

nodes.label: MMA(III)
nodes.detail: Monomethylarsonous acid; trivalent methylated arsenic species. Produced by GSTO1-catalyzed reduction of MMA(V). More toxic than inorganic arsenic; generates ROS, inhibits DNA repair via PARP1, and induces oxidative DNA damage. The rate-limiting toxic metabolite in arsenic methylation pathway.

nodes.label: MMA(V)
nodes.detail: Monomethylarsonic acid; oxidized pentavalent form; GSTO1 reduces back to MMA(III) in rate-limiting step

nodes.label: DMA(V)
nodes.detail: Dimethylarsinic acid; final methylation product; less toxic than MMA; primary urinary excretion form; higher %DMA = more efficient metabolism = lower cancer risk

nodes.label: Cr(III)
nodes.detail: Chromium(III); ultimate intracellular species from Cr(VI) reduction; binds N7-guanine in DNA major groove

nodes.label: Cr(V)
nodes.detail: Chromium(V); transient intermediate during GSH-mediated Cr(VI) reduction; potent ROS generator via Fenton-like chemistry

nodes.label: Ascorbate-Cr(III)
nodes.detail: Ascorbate-Cr(III) complex; formed during ascorbate-mediated Cr(VI) reduction (80-90% of intracellular reduction); precursor to most mutagenic Cr-DNA adduct

nodes.label: Cd-Metallothionein
nodes.detail: Cadmium sequestered by metallothionein; Cd displaces Zn from MT, disrupting Zn-dependent proteins (DNA repair enzymes, p53)

nodes.label: ROS (metal-induced)
nodes.detail: Reactive oxygen species from metal-catalyzed Fenton reactions; superoxide, hydroxyl radical, H2O2; generated by As, Cr(V), Ni, Cd

nodes.label: 8-oxo-dG (8-OHdG)
nodes.detail: 8-Hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-oxo-7,8-dihydro-2'-deoxyguanosine); major oxidative DNA damage marker; causes G:C → T:A transversions; repaired by OGG1/BER. Unified node — formerly split as Oxo_dG (curated showcase) and 8_OHdG (PMID:10417614; PMC3606021).

nodes.label: Binary Cr(III)-DNA
nodes.detail: Cr(III) bound to N7-guanine in major groove; accounts for 75-95% of Cr-DNA bound species in cells with restored ascorbate; weakly mutagenic

nodes.label: Asc-Cr(III)-DNA
nodes.detail: Ternary ascorbate-Cr(III)-DNA crosslink; 31x more mutagenic than binary adduct; ~6% of total Cr-DNA; G/C→T/A transversions (51%), G/C→A/T transitions (30%); processed by error-prone bypass polymerases

nodes.label: Ni-DNA-Protein XL
nodes.detail: Nickel-mediated DNA-protein crosslinks; histone-DNA crosslinks from Ni binding to histone proteins; disrupts chromatin structure and gene expression

nodes.label: Heavy Metal Carcinogenesis
nodes.detail: Composite pathway integrating oxidative stress, metal homeostasis, DNA repair inhibition, and epigenetic modification mechanisms common to carcinogenic metals

nodes.label: Formaldehyde
nodes.detail: Building materials, industrial use, vehicle exhaust; also produced endogenously via one-carbon metabolism. IARC Group 1 carcinogen for nasopharyngeal cancer.
nodes.exposure: inhalation (occupational, indoor air), endogenous metabolism

nodes.label: Acetaldehyde
nodes.detail: Direct-acting aldehyde carcinogen (IARC Group 2B, CAS 75-07-0). Environmental exposure via tobacco smoke, fermented foods, and industrial sources. Forms N2-ethylidene-dG DNA adducts. Distinct from 'acetaldehyde associated with consumption of alcoholic beverages' (Group 1), which is modeled as the intracellular metabolite Acetaldehyde_int (product of ethanol oxidation via ADH1B/ADH1C).
nodes.exposure: tobacco smoke, fermented foods, industrial exposure

nodes.label: TCDD
nodes.detail: 2,3,7,8-Tetrachlorodibenzo-para-dioxin; most potent AhR ligand with picomolar binding affinity. Half-life 7-11 years. Acts as tumor promoter via epigenetic reprogramming, not direct genotoxin.
nodes.exposure: industrial byproduct, incineration, contaminated food (bioaccumulation)

nodes.label: Polychlorinated biphenyls, dioxin-like
nodes.detail: Dioxin-like PCBs (non-ortho and mono-ortho congeners) evaluated as a class by IARC (Vol. 107). Includes PCB-126 (WHO-TEF 0.1), PCB-169 (TEF 0.03), PCB-77 (TEF 0.0001), PCB-118 (TEF 0.00003). Activate AhR pathway; carcinogenicity assessed via toxic equivalency factor (TEF) methodology relative to TCDD.
nodes.exposure: legacy industrial contamination, fish/seafood bioaccumulation, transformer/capacitor oils, breast milk transfer

nodes.label: NDEA
nodes.detail: N-Nitrosodiethylamine; structurally related to NDMA. Found in cured meats, tobacco, and cosmetics. Activated by CYP2E1 alpha-hydroxylation analogous to NDMA pathway.
nodes.exposure: cured meats, tobacco smoke, cosmetics

nodes.label: TCE
nodes.detail: Trichloroethylene; Group 1 carcinogen for kidney cancer. Unique inverted bioactivation: GSTT1-mediated GSH conjugation is the bioactivation pathway (not detoxification), generating renal-toxic metabolites via CCBL1.
nodes.exposure: dry cleaning, metal degreasing, Superfund sites, contaminated groundwater

nodes.label: PCE
nodes.detail: Tetrachloroethylene (perchloroethylene); current dry cleaning solvent. CYP2E1 oxidation to trichloroacetic acid. IARC Group 2A probable carcinogen.
nodes.exposure: dry cleaning (occupational/residential), contaminated water

nodes.label: ALDH2
nodes.detail: Mitochondrial aldehyde dehydrogenase 2; primary acetaldehyde and formaldehyde clearance. rs671 (ALDH2*2): 6-19x acetaldehyde accumulation.

nodes.label: ADH1B
nodes.detail: Alcohol dehydrogenase 1B; oxidizes ethanol to acetaldehyde. ADH1B*2 (rs1229984) fast allele; ESCC OR 2.50 in alcohol consumers.

nodes.label: ADH1C
nodes.detail: Alcohol dehydrogenase 1C (gamma subunit); contributes to ethanol oxidation. rs698 (Ile349Val) modulates catalytic rate.

nodes.label: ADH5
nodes.detail: Formaldehyde dehydrogenase (class III ADH); cytosolic formaldehyde clearance via S-hydroxymethylglutathione pathway.

nodes.label: FANCD2
nodes.detail: Fanconi anemia complementation group D2; repairs acetaldehyde-induced DNA interstrand crosslinks (ICLs).

nodes.label: AHR
nodes.detail: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor; ligand-activated transcription factor. Binds TCDD/dioxin-like compounds and induces CYP1A1/CYP1B1 via XRE elements.

nodes.label: CAR
nodes.detail: Constitutive androstane receptor (NR1I3); ligand-activated nuclear receptor. Activated by non-dioxin-like PCBs, inducing CYP2B/CYP3A and promoting tumor proliferation via xenobiotic metabolism and oxidative stress (IARC Monograph 107).

nodes.label: PXR
nodes.detail: Pregnane X receptor (NR1I2); ligand-activated nuclear receptor. Activated by non-dioxin-like PCBs alongside CAR, inducing CYP3A4 and ABC transporters; promotes hepatocellular proliferation and tumor promotion (IARC Monograph 107).

nodes.label: ARNT
nodes.detail: AhR nuclear translocator (HIF-1beta); obligate co-factor for AhR. Forms AhR-ARNT heterodimer that binds XRE/DRE elements.

nodes.label: AHRR
nodes.detail: AhR repressor; negative feedback regulator. cg05575921 CpG hypomethylation is a validated blood-based biomarker for tobacco/TCDD exposure.

nodes.label: CCBL1
nodes.detail: Cysteine conjugate beta-lyase 1; renal proximal tubule enzyme that bioactivates DCVC to reactive DCVT thiol, causing DNA adducts and VHL mutations. rs2293968/rs2280841/rs2259043/rs941960 tagging SNPs.

nodes.label: Acetaldehyde (intracellular)
nodes.detail: Intracellular acetaldehyde; reactive electrophile that forms DNA adducts and protein cross-links.

nodes.label: Formate
nodes.detail: Terminal product of formaldehyde oxidation; urinary biomarker of formaldehyde exposure.

nodes.label: AhR-ARNT complex
nodes.detail: Active transcription factor heterodimer; binds XRE/DRE elements to induce CYP1A1/CYP1B1. Not a metabolite per se but modeled as an intermediate complex.

nodes.label: Hydroxymethylnitrosamine
nodes.detail: Alpha-hydroxylation product of NDMA/NDEA; proximate carcinogen that spontaneously decomposes to methyldiazonium + formaldehyde.

nodes.label: Methyldiazonium ion
nodes.detail: Reactive methylating species used to represent NDMA alkylation.
nodes.evidence: Reactive methylating species used to represent NDMA alkylation.

nodes.detail: S-(1,2-dichlorovinyl)glutathione; GSTT1 conjugation product of TCE. Transported to kidney for further processing.

nodes.label: DCVC
nodes.detail: S-(1,2-dichlorovinyl)-L-cysteine; renal processing product of DCVG. Substrate for CCBL1 beta-lyase bioactivation.

nodes.label: Chloral hydrate
nodes.detail: CYP2E1 oxidative metabolite of TCE; hepatotoxic intermediate oxidized to trichloroacetic acid.

nodes.label: TCA
nodes.detail: Trichloroacetic acid; stable urinary biomarker for TCE/PCE exposure.

nodes.label: N2-HOMedG
nodes.detail: N2-hydroxymethyl-dG; formaldehyde-DNA adduct. ~20-fold increase in ALDH2/ADH5 double-knockout mice.

nodes.label: N2-ethylidene-dG
nodes.detail: Acetaldehyde-DNA adduct; forms interstrand crosslinks (ICLs) requiring Fanconi anemia pathway repair.

nodes.label: Renal DNA damage
nodes.detail: DCVC-derived DCVT thiol forms DNA adducts in renal proximal tubule; associated with VHL tumor suppressor mutations in renal cell carcinoma.

nodes.label: Aldehyde Carcinogenesis
nodes.detail: Composite pathway covering formaldehyde and acetaldehyde metabolism, DNA adduct formation, and Fanconi anemia repair.

nodes.label: AhR-Mediated Transcriptional Induction
nodes.detail: AhR/ARNT-mediated transcriptional induction of CYP1A1/CYP1B1; tumor promotion via epigenetic reprogramming without direct DNA damage.

nodes.label: N-Nitroso Compound Activation
nodes.detail: CYP2E1/CYP2A6-mediated alpha-hydroxylation pathway for dietary nitrosamines; generates alkylating methyldiazonium ions.

nodes.label: Chlorinated Solvent Dual Pathway
nodes.detail: Dual metabolic pathway: CYP2E1 oxidative (hepatic) and GSTT1 GSH conjugation bioactivation (renal). The GSH pathway is uniquely a bioactivation route.

nodes.label: Ethanol in alcoholic beverages
nodes.detail: Upstream alcohol substrate represented to connect ADH-mediated oxidation to intracellular acetaldehyde formation. Included as a package bridge so the aldehyde pathway resolves in standalone and merged graphs.
nodes.exposure: alcoholic beverages

nodes.label: N2,3-ethenoguanine
nodes.detail: Representative etheno adduct associated with vinyl chloride exposure.
nodes.evidence: Representative etheno adduct associated with vinyl chloride exposure.

provenance.evidence: Representative etheno adduct associated with vinyl chloride exposure.
provenance.citation: Curated DNA adduct entry for N2,3-ethenoguanine

nodes.label: Acrylamide
nodes.detail: Water-soluble vinyl monomer generated by Maillard chemistry in high-temperature cooking of starchy foods (fried/baked potatoes, coffee roasting) and by polyacrylamide manufacture. Bioactivated by CYP2E1 epoxidation to glycidamide, the ultimate mutagen. References: IARC Monograph Vol 60 (1994); Toxicol Sci 2005 (PMID:16141435).
nodes.exposure: high-temperature cooked starchy foods, tobacco smoke, polyacrylamide industry

nodes.label: Glycidamide
nodes.detail: 2,3-Epoxypropanamide; direct-acting epoxide and ultimate mutagenic metabolite of acrylamide. Not separately IARC-evaluated; acrylamide (parent exposure) is Group 2A. Forms N7-(2-carbamoyl-2-hydroxyethyl)-dG and N3-GA-dA DNA adducts. Detoxified by GSTP1/GSTM1 glutathione conjugation.
nodes.exposure: endogenous formation from acrylamide via CYP2E1

nodes.label: Cyclophosphamide
nodes.detail: Oxazaphosphorine prodrug chemotherapeutic. Bioactivated primarily by CYP2B6 (major) and CYP3A4/2C9 (minor) to 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide, which ring-opens to aldophosphamide and fragments to phosphoramide mustard (ultimate DNA-crosslinking agent) plus acrolein. Associated with secondary bladder cancer and therapy-related AML. References: PMID:10348794; PMID:8242617; IARC Monograph Vol 100A (2012).
nodes.exposure: therapeutic chemotherapy (lymphomas, breast cancer, autoimmune disease)

nodes.label: Chlorambucil
nodes.detail: Aromatic nitrogen mustard. Forms aziridinium ion via intramolecular cyclization, yielding N7-guanine monoadducts and G-G interstrand crosslinks. Detoxified by GSTP1 glutathione conjugation. References: PMID:7862715; IARC Monograph Vol 100A (2012).
nodes.exposure: therapeutic chemotherapy (CLL, Waldenstroem macroglobulinemia, ovarian cancer)

nodes.label: Sulfur mustard
nodes.detail: Bis(2-chloroethyl) sulfide. Chemical-warfare vesicant that cyclizes to a reactive episulfonium ion, generating N7-mustard-Gua monoadducts and DNA crosslinks. Linked to lung cancer in exposed workers and veterans. References: PMID:24858262; IARC Monograph Vol 100F (2012).
nodes.exposure: chemical-weapon exposure, legacy ordnance, historic occupational mustard-gas factories

nodes.label: Busulfan
nodes.detail: 1,4-Butanediol dimethanesulfonate; bifunctional alkyl sulfonate used in HSCT conditioning. Hydrolyzes non-enzymatically to a reactive methanesulfonate intermediate, forming N7-(2,3,4-trihydroxybutyl)-dG adducts and DNA-DNA interstrand crosslinks. Detoxified by GSTA1/GSTP1 glutathione conjugation (GSH-Bu). References: PMID:6892995; IARC Monograph Vol 100A (2012).
nodes.exposure: therapeutic chemotherapy (CML, bone-marrow-transplant conditioning)

nodes.label: MNU (N-methyl-N-nitrosourea)
nodes.detail: N-methyl-N-nitrosourea; direct-acting methylating agent requiring no enzymatic activation. Spontaneously decomposes at physiological pH to methyldiazohydroxide/methyldiazonium, alkylating DNA at O6-guanine (G:C to A:T transitions) and N7-guanine. Canonical model carcinogen for MGMT biology. References: Chem Res Toxicol 1991 (PMID:1912317); IARC Monograph Vol 17 (1978).
nodes.exposure: experimental/research reagent; trace formation in cured meats

nodes.label: 4-Hydroxycyclophosphamide
nodes.detail: Primary CYP2B6/CYP3A4 activation product of cyclophosphamide; equilibrates with aldophosphamide and fragments to phosphoramide mustard plus acrolein (PMID:10348794; PMID:8242617).

nodes.label: Phosphoramide mustard
nodes.detail: Ultimate DNA-crosslinking species from cyclophosphamide activation; bifunctional nitrogen mustard that forms G-G interstrand crosslinks via aziridinium intermediates (PMID:9092631).

nodes.label: Chlorambucil aziridinium
nodes.detail: Cyclic aziridinium cation formed by intramolecular cyclization of chlorambucil; alkylates N7-guanine and generates interstrand crosslinks (PMID:7862715).

nodes.label: Sulfur-mustard episulfonium ion
nodes.detail: Cyclic sulfonium intermediate formed by intramolecular cyclization of sulfur mustard; ultimate electrophile for N7-Gua monoadducts and DNA crosslinks (PMID:24858262).

nodes.label: Busulfan methanesulfonate intermediate
nodes.detail: Reactive bifunctional alkylator generated by hydrolytic displacement of methanesulfonate groups from busulfan; yields N7-THPG adducts and DNA-DNA interstrand crosslinks (PMID:6892995).

nodes.label: N7-GA-dG
nodes.detail: N7-(2-carbamoyl-2-hydroxyethyl)-2'-deoxyguanosine; dominant glycidamide-DNA adduct from acrylamide exposure. Depurinates to abasic sites handled through BER (PMID:7767980; PMID:17234719).

nodes.label: N7-methyl-dG
nodes.detail: N7-methyl-2'-deoxyguanosine; most abundant methylation lesion from MNU and temozolomide via methyldiazonium. Non-mutagenic itself but labile; depurinates to abasic sites repaired by BER (XRCC1 scaffold).

nodes.label: G-G interstrand crosslink (mustard-type)
nodes.detail: Bifunctional N7-alkyl-dG interstrand crosslink generated by phosphoramide mustard (cyclophosphamide), chlorambucil aziridinium, sulfur-mustard episulfonium, and the busulfan methanesulfonate intermediate. Requires Fanconi-anemia/HR repair; mechanistic basis for therapeutic cytotoxicity (PMID:9092631, PMID:7862715, PMID:24858262, PMID:6892995).

nodes.label: Alkylating Agent Carcinogenesis
nodes.detail: Composite pathway covering direct-acting methylators (MNU), prodrug-activated alkylators (cyclophosphamide, temozolomide), chemical-warfare mustards (sulfur mustard), bifunctional sulfonates (busulfan), and CYP2E1-activated acrylamide/glycidamide converging on N7/O6-guanine adducts and DNA interstrand crosslinks.

nodes.label: Urethane (ethyl carbamate)
nodes.detail: Ethyl carbamate; natural contaminant of fermented foods and alcoholic beverages, especially stone-fruit brandies, sake, sherry, and bread crust. CYP2E1 dehydrogenates urethane to vinyl carbamate, which is then re-epoxidized to vinyl carbamate epoxide — the ultimate mutagen that forms etheno-A/etheno-C DNA adducts (same adduct family as vinyl chloride). References: J Pharmacol Exp Ther 2003 (PMID:12704224); Chem Res Toxicol 2010 (PMID:20205516); IARC Monograph Vol 96 (2010).
nodes.exposure: alcoholic beverages (stone-fruit brandies, sake, sherry), fermented foods, bread crust

nodes.label: Acrolein
nodes.detail: 2-Propenal; smallest alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde and potent Michael acceptor. Major constituent of cigarette smoke, heated cooking oils, and automobile exhaust. Forms alpha/gamma-OH-1,N2-propano-dG (Acr-dG) exocyclic adducts, which are mispairing, bulky lesions repaired by NER/BER. Detoxified by GSTP1 (GS-HPMA) and ALDH2 oxidation to acrylic acid. Also generated endogenously as a metabolite of cyclophosphamide (see Acrolein_CP node). References: IARC Monograph Vol 128 (2021); Chem Res Toxicol 2009 (PMID:19397281).
nodes.exposure: tobacco smoke, heated cooking oils, wildfire/vehicle exhaust

nodes.label: Acrolein (cyclophosphamide metabolite)
nodes.detail: Acrolein generated endogenously as the obligate byproduct of 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide/aldophosphamide beta-elimination during cyclophosphamide bioactivation. Not separately IARC-evaluated; parent cyclophosphamide is Group 1. Same chemical species as exogenous acrolein (Acrolein node) but sourced from chemotherapy metabolism. Drives hemorrhagic cystitis and contributes to secondary bladder cancer risk. Forms alpha/gamma-OH-1,N2-propano-dG (Acr-dG) adducts. Detoxified by GSTP1 and ALDH2. References: PMID:10348794; IARC Monograph Vol 100A (2012).

nodes.label: Crotonaldehyde
nodes.detail: (E)-2-Butenal; alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde abundant in tobacco smoke, alcoholic beverages (congener), and heated cooking oils. Forms cyclic 1,N2-propano-dG (Cr-dG) exocyclic adducts via Michael addition/cyclization; adducts are miscoding and persist in liver, oral mucosa, and lung tissue. References: PMID:2736720; IARC Monograph Vol 63 (1995).
nodes.exposure: tobacco smoke, alcoholic beverages, heated cooking oils, air pollutant

nodes.label: Furfural
nodes.detail: Furan-2-carbaldehyde; Maillard-reaction aldehyde abundant in roasted coffee, beer, bread, and heated fruit products. Modeled via an HMF/SMF activation branch: SULT1A1 converts 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 5-sulfoxymethylfurfural (SMF), a DNA-reactive electrophile that alkylates dA/dG. Classified IARC Group 3 but included for mechanistic completeness of dietary aldehyde exposures. References: Chem Res Toxicol 2012 (PMID:22563731); Food Chem Toxicol 2015 (PMID:26454887); EFSA CONTAM Panel Opinion 2011.
nodes.exposure: roasted coffee, beer, bread, heated fruit/sugar products

nodes.label: Malondialdehyde (MDA)
nodes.detail: Propanedial; ubiquitous lipid-peroxidation end-product and a direct-acting mutagen. Universal biomarker of oxidative stress. Reacts with dG to form pyrimido[1,2-a]purin-10(3H)-one (M1-dG), a miscoding adduct that causes base substitutions and frameshifts. Elevated in chronic inflammation, alcoholic liver disease, and hepatocarcinogenesis. References: Marnett 1999 (PMID:10064852); Niedernhofer et al., J Biol Chem 2003 (PMID:12775726).
nodes.exposure: endogenous lipid peroxidation, oxidative stress, chronic inflammation

nodes.label: 4-Hydroxynonenal (4-HNE)
nodes.detail: (E)-4-Hydroxy-2-nonenal; the most reactive major product of omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty-acid peroxidation. Not IARC-evaluated; endogenous lipid peroxidation product. Bifunctional Michael acceptor that forms exocyclic 1,N2-propano-dG (HNE-dG) adducts, preferentially at methylated CpG sites (a molecular link between oxidative stress and TP53 hotspot mutations). Detoxified by GSTP1 glutathione conjugation and ALDH2 oxidation. References: Esterbauer, Schaur & Zollner, Free Radic Biol Med 1991 (PMID:1937131); Hu et al., Carcinogenesis 2002 (PMID:12419825).
nodes.exposure: endogenous omega-6 lipid peroxidation, oxidative stress, alcoholic steatohepatitis

nodes.label: Vinyl carbamate
nodes.detail: CYP2E1-derived dehydrogenation product of urethane; proximal intermediate re-epoxidized to vinyl carbamate epoxide (PMID:12704224).

nodes.label: Vinyl carbamate epoxide
nodes.detail: Ultimate mutagenic metabolite of urethane; alkylates dA and dC to yield etheno-DNA adducts equivalent to those formed by vinyl chloride (PMID:20205516).

nodes.label: 5-sulfoxymethylfurfural (SMF)
nodes.detail: Reactive sulfate ester generated from HMF by SULT1A1; DNA-reactive electrophile that alkylates dA/dG (PMID:22563731; PMID:26454887).

nodes.label: alpha/gamma-OH-PdG (Acr-dG)
nodes.detail: alpha- and gamma-hydroxy-1,N2-propano-2'-deoxyguanosine; major Michael-addition adduct from acrolein reacting at N1/N2 of guanine. Miscoding in ring-opened form; repaired by NER with XRCC1/BER backup (PMID:19397281).

nodes.label: N-(deoxyguanosin-8-yl)-benzidine
nodes.detail: Major DNA adduct formed from N-hydroxy-benzidine via nitrenium ion; detected in bladder urothelium of aromatic amine-exposed workers. Miscoding lesion causing G→T transversions. Repaired by NER.

nodes.label: Cr-1,N2-PdG (Cr-dG)
nodes.detail: Cyclic 1,N2-propano-dG adduct from crotonaldehyde Michael addition; miscoding adduct detected in liver, oral mucosa, and lung of smokers (IARC Monograph Vol 63; PMID:2736720).

nodes.label: M1-dG (pyrimido-purinone)
nodes.detail: 3-(2'-deoxy-beta-D-erythro-pentofuranosyl)pyrimido[1,2-a]purin-10(3H)-one; principal MDA-DNA adduct. Miscoding lesion causing base substitutions and frameshifts; basal levels in healthy tissues provide a baseline for oxidative-stress-driven mutagenesis (PMID:10064852).

nodes.label: SMF-deoxyadenosine adduct
nodes.detail: N6-(2-furoylmethyl)-deoxyadenosine; DNA adduct formed by 5-sulfoxymethylfurfural (SMF) alkylation at N6 of deoxyadenosine. Also forms dG adducts. Detected in liver of HMF/SMF-exposed animals. Biomarker of Maillard reaction product genotoxicity.

nodes.label: HNE-1,N2-PdG (HNE-dG)
nodes.detail: Exocyclic 1,N2-propano-dG adduct from 4-HNE Michael addition/cyclization; formation is strongly enhanced at methylated CpG sites, mechanistically linking lipid peroxidation to TP53 hotspot mutations (PMID:1937131; PMID:12419825).

nodes.label: Polychlorinated biphenyls, non-dioxin like
nodes.detail: Non-dioxin-like (NDL) PCBs evaluated as a class by IARC (Vol. 107). Includes PCB-153 and PCB-138, the most abundant PCBs in human tissues. Activate CAR/PXR and RyR rather than AhR; tumor promoters via oxidative stress and gap-junction inhibition.
nodes.exposure: fatty fish, meat, dairy; breast milk transfer; highly persistent; adipose storage, transplacental transfer

nodes.label: 2,3,4,7,8-PeCDF
nodes.detail: 2,3,4,7,8-Pentachlorodibenzofuran; most potent non-TCDD AhR ligand with WHO-TEF 0.3. Major contributor to Yusho/Yu-cheng poisoning TEQ and dominant PCDF in human adipose (IARC Monograph 100F).
nodes.exposure: PCB combustion, rice-oil contamination (Yusho/Yu-cheng), incineration

nodes.label: Hexachlorobenzene (HCB)
nodes.detail: Persistent organochlorine fungicide and industrial byproduct; weak AhR agonist and CYP1A1/CYP1B1 inducer. Linked to hepatic porphyria, thyroid cancer, and elevated breast-cancer risk (IARC Monograph 79).
nodes.exposure: legacy fungicide residues, chlorinated solvent manufacture, dietary fat

nodes.label: Lindane (γ-HCH)
nodes.detail: Gamma-hexachlorocyclohexane; organochlorine insecticide classified Group 1 by IARC in 2015 (Monograph 113) based on non-Hodgkin lymphoma evidence. Acts via CAR/PXR-mediated CYP2B/CYP3A induction, GABA-A receptor antagonism, and oxidative stress.
nodes.exposure: legacy agricultural insecticide, head-lice pharmaceutical, persistent in soil and food chain

nodes.label: DDT
nodes.detail: Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane; classified Group 2A by IARC in 2015 (Monograph 113) based on liver, testicular, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma evidence. Primarily CAR/PXR-mediated tumor promoter; weak AhR activity. Dechlorinated to DDE via CYP2B-mediated metabolism.
nodes.exposure: legacy agricultural/vector-control insecticide, global body-burden biomarker

nodes.label: Pentachlorophenol (PCP)
nodes.detail: Chlorinated phenol wood preservative and biocide; classified Group 1 by IARC in 2019 (Monograph 117) based on non-Hodgkin lymphoma and multiple myeloma evidence. AhR agonist with redox-cycling tetrachloro-p-benzoquinone metabolite; often co-contaminated with dioxins/furans.
nodes.exposure: sawmill/lumber workers, treated wood products, contaminated soil and groundwater

nodes.label: Chlordane (technical)
nodes.detail: Technical-grade cyclodiene insecticide mixture; classified Group 2B by IARC in 1991 (Monograph 53). Primarily CAR/PXR activator; liver tumor promoter in rodents; persists in indoor dust from historic termiticide applications.
nodes.exposure: legacy subterranean termiticide, indoor dust residues, dietary bioaccumulation

nodes.label: Heptachlor
nodes.detail: Cyclodiene insecticide co-formulated with chlordane; classified Group 2B by IARC in 1991 (Monograph 53). Bioactivated to more toxic heptachlor epoxide by hepatic CYPs; CAR/PXR-mediated tumor promotion.
nodes.exposure: legacy termiticide, soil/sediment residues, dietary exposure via meat and dairy

nodes.label: Toxaphene
nodes.detail: Complex chlorinated camphene mixture (~670 congeners); classified Group 2B by IARC in 2001 (Monograph 79). Mixed CAR/PXR and weak AhR agonism; GABA-A antagonism; long-range atmospheric transport to Arctic food webs.
nodes.exposure: post-DDT-ban cotton insecticide, persistent in fish/marine mammals, Arctic bioaccumulation

nodes.detail: MutL homolog 1; mismatch repair of replication errors past DNA adducts

nodes.label: Lead compounds, inorganic
nodes.detail: IARC Group 2A (Vol 87, 2006). Inorganic lead compounds (oxides, salts). 30-year bone half-life. Inhibits ALAD (heme synthesis), displaces zinc in DNA repair proteins. Target: kidney, brain, blood. Metallic lead is Group 2B (separate node); organic lead compounds are Group 3 (separate node).
nodes.exposure: Lead smelting, battery recycling, paint, plumbing, ammunition

nodes.label: Lead, metallic
nodes.detail: IARC Group 2B (Vol 23, Suppl. 7, 1987). Metallic lead evaluated separately from inorganic lead compounds. Same bone accumulation and ALAD inhibition mechanism, but weaker carcinogenicity evidence.
nodes.exposure: Lead smelting, sheet lead, radiation shielding

nodes.label: Lead compounds, organic
nodes.detail: IARC Group 3 (Vol 87, 2006). Organolead compounds (tetraethyl lead, tetramethyl lead). Not classifiable. Note: organic lead is metabolized to ionic lead, which exerts same toxicity as inorganic lead (IARC Vol 87).
nodes.exposure: Leaded gasoline (historical), PVC stabilizers

nodes.label: Methylmercury compounds
nodes.detail: IARC Group 2B (Vol 58, 1993). Methylmercury is the primary toxic species; transported as methylmercury-cysteine complex via LAT1. 70-day half-life. Target: brain, kidney. Inorganic mercury is Group 3 (separate node).
nodes.exposure: Contaminated fish/seafood, biomethylation in aquatic systems

nodes.label: Mercury and inorganic mercury compounds
nodes.detail: IARC Group 3 (Vol 58, 1993). Metallic mercury and inorganic mercury compounds (Hg2+, Hg2 2+). High thiol affinity; binds GSH, metallothionein (MT1A), selenoproteins (SEPP1). Inhibits GPx. Target: brain, kidney.
nodes.exposure: Dental amalgam, chlor-alkali industry, gold mining, thermometers

nodes.label: Cobalt metal (without tungsten carbide)
nodes.detail: IARC Group 2A (Vol 131, 2023). Cobalt metal upgraded from Group 2B. Releases Co2+ ions in vivo, mimicking hypoxia via EGLN1 inhibition. Target: lung, thyroid. Soluble cobalt(II) salts also Group 2A; cobalt(II) oxide is Group 2B (separate node).
nodes.exposure: Hard metal tools, carbide manufacturing, hip prostheses

nodes.label: Cobalt(II) oxide
nodes.detail: IARC Group 2B (Vol 131, 2023). Cobalt(II) oxide. Sufficient evidence in animals. Lower bioavailability than cobalt metal or soluble salts; different mechanism profile.
nodes.exposure: Pigment production, ceramic industry, catalyst manufacturing

nodes.label: Trivalent antimony compounds
nodes.detail: IARC Group 2A (Vol 131, 2023). Trivalent antimony (SbIII) has sufficient evidence in animals and strong mechanistic evidence. Often co-toxic with arsenic; interacts with GSTO1. Target: lung, heart, liver.
nodes.exposure: Flame retardants, semiconductors, glass manufacturing

nodes.label: ALAD
nodes.detail: Delta-aminolevulinic acid dehydratase. Primary lead target. Inhibition causes delta-ALA accumulation and ROS.

nodes.label: SEPP1
nodes.detail: Selenoprotein P. Protective against mercury toxicity via selenium antagonism.

nodes.label: EGLN1 (PHD2)
nodes.detail: Prolyl hydroxylase domain 2. Inhibited by cobalt, stabilizing HIF-1α (hypoxia mimicry).

nodes.label: Glutathione peroxidase
nodes.detail: Selenoprotein; mercury inhibits selenol-dependent activity.

nodes.label: DMT1 (SLC11A2)
nodes.detail: Divalent metal transporter 1. Major entry route for lead (shared with iron).

nodes.label: LAT1 (SLC7A5)
nodes.detail: L-type amino acid transporter 1. Methylmercury-cysteine complex mimicry entry.

nodes.label: ZIP14 (SLC39A14)
nodes.detail: Zinc/iron permease 14. Transports non-transferrin bound cobalt and iron.

nodes.label: Delta-ALA
nodes.detail: Delta-aminolevulinic acid. Accumulates with lead exposure. Auto-oxidizes generating ROS.

nodes.label: Methylmercury-GSH
nodes.detail: Methylmercury-glutathione complex. Transported and excreted.

nodes.label: Co(II)
nodes.detail: Cobalt(II) ion. Redox active, participates in Fenton-like reactions.

nodes.label: Glutathione
nodes.detail: Major cellular antioxidant; depleted by lead and mercury binding.

nodes.label: Aristolochic acid
nodes.detail: Plant alkaloid represented through nitroreduction to a reactive N-acylnitrenium ion and deoxyadenosine adduct formation.
nodes.evidence: Plant alkaloid represented through nitroreduction to a reactive N-acylnitrenium ion and deoxyadenosine adduct formation.
nodes.exposure: Traditional herbal medicines (Aristolochia species), contaminated food crops (Balkan endemic nephropathy)

nodes.detail: Reactive cyclic N-acylnitrenium ion formed by nitroreduction of aristolochic acid.

nodes.detail: Canonical aristolochic acid-derived deoxyadenosine adduct; associated with A:T to T:A transversion mutations.
nodes.evidence: Canonical aristolochic acid-derived deoxyadenosine adduct; associated with A:T to T:A transversion mutations.

nodes.label: Aristolochic Acid Nitroreduction and Adduct Formation
nodes.detail: Composite pathway covering CYP1A1/2 and NQO1-mediated nitroreduction, N-acylnitrenium ion formation, and deoxyadenosine adduct generation.

nodes.label: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA)
nodes.detail: Perfluoroalkyl substance; activator of multiple nuclear receptors including PPARα, CAR, and PXR (with suggestive PPARγ activation in human primary cells). IARC could not identify a common specific mechanism; multiple mechanisms are possible or likely. Five Key Characteristics cited: KC4 (epigenetic alterations), KC5 (oxidative stress), KC7 (immunosuppression), KC8 (receptor-mediated effects), KC10 (alters cell proliferation, cell death, or nutrient supply). The primary in-human basis for Group 1 was KC4 and KC7 — IARC reached Group 1 particularly in the absence of strong evidence in exposed humans for genotoxicity (KC2) or receptor-mediated effects (KC8). Group 1 based on limited evidence in humans (renal cell carcinoma, cancer of the testis), sufficient evidence in experimental animals (one GLP rat study, both sexes), and strong mechanistic evidence in exposed humans, human primary cells, and experimental systems.
nodes.evidence: Perfluoroalkyl substance; activator of multiple nuclear receptors (PPARα, CAR, PXR, suggestive PPARγ). IARC cited five KCs (KC4, KC5, KC7, KC8, KC10); primary in-human basis was KC4 (epigenetic) and KC7 (immunosuppression), not receptor-mediated effects.
nodes.exposure: Contaminated drinking water, food packaging, textiles, firefighting foam, fluoropolymer manufacture

provenance.evidence: Perfluoroalkyl substance; activator of multiple nuclear receptors. Group 1 based on limited human evidence (renal cell carcinoma, testicular cancer), sufficient animal evidence (one GLP rat study, both sexes), and strong mechanistic evidence (KC4/KC7 in exposed humans).

nodes.label: Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS)
nodes.detail: Perfluoroalkyl substance; activator of multiple nuclear receptors including PPARα, CAR, and PXR. IARC could not identify a common specific mechanism. Five Key Characteristics cited (same framework as PFOA): KC4, KC5, KC7, KC8, KC10. Group 2B based on inadequate evidence in humans, limited evidence in experimental animals (one GLP rat study, female sex), and strong mechanistic evidence including in exposed humans.
nodes.evidence: Perfluoroalkyl substance; activator of multiple nuclear receptors (PPARα, CAR, PXR). IARC cited five KCs (KC4, KC5, KC7, KC8, KC10). Group 2B based on inadequate human evidence, limited animal evidence (one GLP rat study, female sex), and strong mechanistic evidence.
nodes.exposure: Firefighting foam (AFFF), semiconductor fabrication, food packaging, contaminated water

nodes.label: PPARα
nodes.detail: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha; ligand-activated nuclear receptor. One of multiple receptors activated by PFOA/PFOS (alongside CAR, PXR, suggestive PPARγ). IARC treats receptor activation as a mechanism that 'might contribute' to hepatocarcinogenicity in rodents but did not identify it as the primary carcinogenic driver.

nodes.label: Ultraviolet radiation (UVA, UVB, UVC)
nodes.detail: Physical agent; directly damages DNA through photodimer formation (cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers and 6-4 photoproducts) and oxidative stress. No metabolic activation required. Group 1 for skin cancers (melanoma, squamous cell, basal cell) and ocular melanoma.

nodes.exposure: Solar radiation, tanning devices, welding arcs

nodes.label: Cyclobutane pyrimidine dimer (CPD)
nodes.detail: Most common UV-induced DNA lesion; forms covalent bonds between adjacent pyrimidines on the same DNA strand. Causes C to T and CC to TT signature mutations.

nodes.label: 6-4 photoproduct
nodes.detail: Second most common UV-induced DNA lesion; covalent linkage between positions 6 and 4 of adjacent pyrimidines. Less frequent than CPD but more mutagenic.

nodes.label: Ionizing radiation (all types)
nodes.detail: Physical agent covering X- and gamma-radiation, neutron radiation (Group 1 on mechanistic evidence; inadequate human evidence per Vol. 100D p. 237), and internally deposited alpha-emitters (radon-222, radium-224/226/228, plutonium-239) and beta-emitters (I-131, P-32, Thorotrast, Sr-90). Damages DNA directly through double-strand breaks, single-strand breaks, and oxidative base damage via radiolysis of water. No metabolic activation required. Group 1; X/gamma-radiation has 13 sufficient-evidence cancer sites per Vol. 100D p. 210; at least 17 distinct sites across all ionizing-radiation subtypes.
nodes.evidence: Physical agent covering all ionizing radiation types. Damages DNA directly through double-strand breaks and oxidative stress. No metabolic activation required.
nodes.exposure: Medical imaging and radiotherapy, occupational (nuclear, mining, aerospace), environmental background, nuclear accidents

provenance.evidence: Ionizing radiation (all types) classified as Group 1. Covers X/gamma, neutrons, alpha- and beta-emitting radionuclides.

nodes.label: Radon-222 and its decay products
nodes.detail: Naturally occurring radioactive gas from uranium-238 decay chain. Alpha-emitting decay products (Po-218, Po-214) deliver localized high-LET dose to bronchial epithelium. Leading cause of lung cancer among never-smokers; second-leading cause of lung-cancer death after smoking in Europe and North America (8-15% attributable, Vol. 100D p. 248). Group 1 for lung cancer.
nodes.evidence: Naturally occurring radioactive gas; alpha-emitting decay products deliver high-LET dose to bronchial epithelium. Leading cause of lung cancer among never-smokers; second-leading cause after smoking in Europe and North America (Vol. 100D p. 248).
nodes.exposure: Residential indoor radon gas (geological uranium), occupational (uranium mining, underground work)
